_comment: CLASSICAL progressions. Chord progressions are unprotectable and freely copyable (SAS v. Sheeran, 2d Cir. 2024) regardless of era, so these are the real harmonic patterns of the encoded pieces: the Pachelbel ground, the lament/chaconne, the baroque circle-of-fifths sequence, the harmonic-minor cadence, the tonic pedal that the ostinato hooks sit on, and the deceptive V-bVI. Harmonic-minor tell: V is MAJOR/dom7 in every minor progression here (quality override '7') so the leading tone survives -- a modal b7 cadence is the single biggest classical corny trap. Degrees are diatonic 1-7 in the stated mode (natural minor: 6 = bVI, 7 = bVII). bII (Neapolitan) is not expressible in the degree vocabulary yet, so the Moonlight-style loop substitutes iv for bII6.
